top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a mature, independently confirmed achievement with a clean two-name allocation: the magic-wavelength lattice is a genuine concept distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes, 1e-18 performance is confirmed by cross-laboratory comparisons in Sr, Yb and Hg, and it has already delivered bounds on varying constants and relativistic tests. P002 adds a one-name IceCube credit that I find hard to defend, so it ranks second as it keeps the sound clock half; twisted bilayer graphene is promising but its mechanism is unsettled and attribution is contested; topological insulators ride on the already-honoured 2016 topic and a hard three-name cut; no award is worst since a mature, well-attributed achievement exists.
recusal_note: Documented connections to the clock candidates are not apparent, but my long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and attosecond/optical-physics colleagues in AMO means I am close to the field; no direct tie to Katori or Ye, and none to the other credited names is apparent from the profile.
